incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — pop-us-east1 edge -> CDN transit: sustained packet loss / route oscillation detected for multiple customer prefixes. Initial severity: P2. Paging on-call.

Em (oncall): ack — taking it. Jumping in to triage. Any immediate customer-reported pages? @cs-bot what's the customer impact summary?

cs-bot: 15:03 UTC — Several customers in us-east report 502/timeout spikes and increased tail latency. Approx 12% of requests to affected POP are failing or timing out. No billing impact reported. Links: https://status.internal/incident/2087654321

Raj (neteng): I'm on transit. Observing BGP session churn with TransitA (AS64501) -> intermittent withdraws for our /24s; some paths suddenly prefer TransitB then drop. Router logs show flap on peering with TransitA at 15:01 UTC. Suspect transit-side policy flapping or community-based reroute.

Em (oncall): can you paste a quick traceroute and BGP summary? need to decide fallback while we investigate.

Raj (neteng): traceroute to one affected prefix:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.12.0.1  0.42 ms  0.39 ms  0.36 ms
 2  198.51.100.2  1.18 ms  1.15 ms  1.11 ms
 3  203.0.113.1  12.3 ms  50.8 ms  200.9 ms   <-- next-hop oscillating
```
BGP summary snippet:
```
Neighbor        AS      Up/Down  Prefixes  LastChange
192.0.2.1       64501   00:00:34    120     00:00:34  (flapping)
192.0.2.2       64502   12:34:12    118     12:34:12
```
Symptoms line up with TransitA withdrawing and TransitB intermittently accepting.

Sara (sre): customer impact = timeouts and 5xx for edge-cached content and API proxying. Rolling fallback to backup transit would reduce errors but may increase latency for some flows. Want to coordinate change window.

Mike (eng-infra): we can programmatically steer POP egress via our traffic-engine rules. Two options: (1) temporarily prepending AS-path to prefer TransitB, or (2) announce more-specifics via secondary uplinks for affected prefixes. Option (1) faster, reversible.

Em (oncall): do (1) — prepend on TransitA so TransitB becomes preferred. Raj, can you run the change and monitor? Keep change scoped to pop-us-east1.

Raj (neteng): making the AS-path prepend now on router edge1-us-east1. Command applied:
```
set policy route-map PREPEND-TRANSITA permit 10
 set as-path prepend 64550 64550 64550
apply to peering TransitA
```

Raj (neteng): applied at 15:12 UTC. Watching BGP table and packet metrics.

Em (oncall): monitoring metrics dashboard. latency and error-rate panels updating... :eyes:

cs-bot: 15:14 UTC — customer error rate decreased from 12% -> 2% within 2 minutes of change. Some customers still see intermittent issues (~1-2%).

Mike (eng-infra): good signal. keep monitoring for 10 minutes then decide whether to keep prepend or attempt restore once TransitA stabilizes.

Raj (neteng): BGP updates have calmed. No more withdraws seen for 60s. TransitA support ticket opened (TS-78944) — they reported an upstream flap in their peering fabric and are investigating.

Em (oncall): handoff incoming — I need to step away for a call at 15:25 UTC. Sara, can you take lead for incident until TransitA confirms stable? Leaving notes in the incident doc.

Sara (sre): taking over. Em — good run. I'll keep the prepend in place for now and set a 30m re-eval. Notifying CS and updating status page.

cs-bot: status page updated: "Degraded connectivity affecting customers in us-east; mitigation in place; working with transit provider." Public timeline link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2087654321

Raj (neteng): added monitoring alert: if withdraws resume send page to neteng-critical.

Em (oncall): quick follow-ups in the thread: confirm list of affected prefixes, capture router-core logs, and schedule postmortem to review fallback automation.

Mike (eng-infra): we'll add a runbook action item: automatic temporary prepend for POP-level transit flaps if error-rate > 8% and withdraws detected. PR for runbook edits: https://git.internal/repo/runbooks/pull/456

Sara (sre): 15:45 UTC — TransitA reported they fixed the fabric and removed the incorrect outbound filter. We're seeing stable adjacency and balanced paths again. Suggest: remove prepend, watch for 15m.

Raj (neteng): removing AS-path prepend on edge1-us-east1 at 15:47 UTC.

cs-bot: 15:50 UTC — customer error rate stable at baseline. Closing mitigation window. Will mark incident as "mitigated, monitoring" and follow up with full postmortem.

Sara (sre): assigning action items: (1) Neteng to confirm root cause with TransitA (TS-78944). (2) Eng-infra to add automated detection + prepend runbook. (3) SRE to run a customer-impact audit and update postmortem. I'll create the incident ticket and assign owners.

Em (oncall): thanks team. Nice small-window mitigation. If any regression, re-open and page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 2087654321 status -> mitigated (15:50 UTC). Postmortem in progress.

[end of thread]
